name_note: GTDB places Clostridium innocuum and a few unnamed relatives in the genus Clostridium_AQ, a split from the classical genus Clostridium, so the literature name used here is Clostridium innocuum.

sentences.text: Clostridium innocuum is an anaerobic, gram-positive, spore-forming bacterium and a commensal member of the human gut microbiome.
A study reported that it is increasingly detected in patients with Clostridioides difficile infection, particularly following vancomycin treatment, with delayed clinical recovery and poor outcomes.
Reports have also associated the organism with extra-intestinal infections, antibiotic-associated diarrhea and inflammatory bowel disease.
Bacteremia has been described, including a case complicating a foot ulcer, and a systematic review of previously reported bacteremia cases found their number limited.
